subject: Escrowed reserve and termination rights proposal — Brightleaf Health
messages:
From: Kimberly Dawson <kimberly.dawson@brightleafhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightleafhealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance reserve / termination rights — initial ask

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the call this morning. As we discussed internally, Brightleaf needs stronger contractual levers than credits alone for mission-critical telemetry and patient-facing workflows. High-level asks:

- Escrowed performance reserve: holdback equal to 3 months of subscription fees at contract signing (drawn only after cure fails).
- Stepwise termination: right to terminate for convenience after either (a) 3 Sev 1 outages in 90 days, or (b) 1 Sev 1 plus repeated latency degradations that materially impact throughput.
- Liquidated-damage style cap: if termination occurs for performance reasons, allow recovery of the escrow + a buyout equal to 30% of the remaining committed value (we view credits as insufficient for repeat failures).

We appreciate Redwood's platform but cannot accept credits as the only remedy given regulatory risk and downstream patient impact. I've attached our Feb SLO report and a short procurement timeline — procurement is on a hard deadline the week of Mar 20.

Attachments: Brightleaf_SLO_report_Feb2028.pdf, Procurement_MA-Timeline.xlsx

Can you confirm whether Redwood can agree in principle and what concessions you'd need?

Thanks,
Kimberly Dawson
Director, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Brightleaf Health

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Kimberly Dawson <kimberly.dawson@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance reserve / termination rights — initial ask

Kimberly — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. We understand the concern and the procurement timeline. High-level response and suggested path:

1) Escrowed holdback: we're open to a conditional holdback mechanism, but we'd prefer it be capped at a defined amount and only releasable after a structured cure/fix process. We typically propose a staged holdback (drawn only after failure to cure following Tiered remediation).

2) Termination triggers: we can agree to termination rights tied to repeated severity-1 events, but need clear definitions (what counts as "Sev 1", measurement window, and whether brief, unrelated network outages count).

3) Buyout / damages: Redwood does not accept uncapped liquidated damages. We can negotiate a buyout formula capped at a multiple of monthly fees (e.g., up to 6 months of fees) and preserve indemnities for data loss.

Next steps I propose: Marissa (CS) and Aditya (Product) to draft an operational SLO table + proposed cure cadence; Lauren to draft legal language for an escrowed holdback and termination threshold. We'll turn a single redline back to you by EOD Thu (Mar 15) so you have time before procurement's deadline.

Is a 3-month escrow holdback (instead of 6) and a 30-day cure window something Brightleaf would consider as a starting compromise?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood proposed contract language — escrow, cure, and termination

Kimberly / team,

Following Sean's note, attached is a redline that implements a middle-ground approach. Key legal points from Redwood's perspective:

- Escrow/holdback: agree to a contractual holdback equal to up to 3 months of committed subscription fees deposited with a mutually acceptable escrow agent. Funds may be drawn only after (i) Customer provides written notice of breach, (ii) Redwood is given a 30-day cure period, and (iii) a mutually agreed independent technical review confirms an uncured SLO violation.

- Termination triggers: agree to termination for material, repeated performance failures, defined as either (A) three Severity 1 incidents within any rolling 90-day window, or (B) a single Severity 1 incident that also results in a verified data integrity loss or regulatory impact.

- Remedies cap: Redwood will agree to a commercial exit buyout capped at six months of subscription fees (subject to mutual audit). We cannot agree to percentage-of-remaining-contract buyouts or open-ended liquidated damages; those create unacceptable operational and financial risk for our customers and Redwood alike.

- Exclusions & carve-outs: events caused by customer misconfiguration, force majeure, third-party infrastructure outages beyond Redwood's control, or non-production testing will be excluded from triggers.

- Operational mitigations: we propose an SLA governance process — 48-hour interim response, runbook activation within 12 hours for Sev 1, post-incident RCA within 10 business days, and 30-day joint remediation plan.

I've attached the redline for your procurement/legal team (Redwood_legal_redline.docx). We tried to balance Brightleaf's risk appetite with Redwood's need for predictable commercial exposure.

If these principals look acceptable, we'll convert into a commercial term sheet for signatures.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: Redwood_legal_redline.docx)

Team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. A few counterpoints from procurement/legal:

- Escrow amount: Brightleaf will accept a 3-month holdback only if the buyout formula is at least 30% of remaining committed value OR an option to recover the holdback plus a capped buyout equal to 3 months of fees. We cannot accept a cap that effectively reduces recovery below material compensation for repeated outages.

- Termination windows: we can agree to define Sev 1, but need the triggers to include latency degradations that materially degrade throughput (we'll provide representative KPIs).

- Cure period: 30 days is a long window for patient-facing services. Can you consider a 14-day cure for repeat severe events with an accelerated arbitration step if remediation stalls?

Attached is an updated timeline and a short note from our security team. Procurement needs a commercial term sheet by Mon Mar 20 to keep the board approval schedule.

Procurement — Brightleaf Health

Kimberly / procurement team — thanks for the quick reply and the clarity on your board timeline. Proposed compromise for the commercial term sheet (for your review):

- Escrowed holdback: 3 months of subscription fees deposited with escrow agent. Release mechanics: (i) Customer notice; (ii) 14-day accelerated cure for repeat severe events (we'll agree on technical criteria), (iii) independent technical verifier confirms uncured SLO violation; funds may be drawn post-confirmation.

- Termination triggers: 3 Sev 1 incidents within a rolling 90-day window OR a single Sev 1 with verified data loss/regulatory impact. Sev 1 definition and latency KPI thresholds to be jointly defined and appended to the SLO schedule.

- Remedies cap: exit buyout capped at 6 months of subscription fees. If Customer prefers a buyout expressed as a % of remaining term, we can offer up to 30% of remaining committed value as an alternate cap (mutually exclusive — pick one).

- Cure & governance: 14-day cure for repeat events, runbook activation within 12 hours, 48-hour interim response, RCA within 7 business days for Sev 1, and mandatory bi-weekly remediation sync until cured.

Next steps: we'll convert this compromise into a commercial term sheet + SLO appendix and circulate by Fri EOD (Mar 16). Please confirm whether Brightleaf can accept the 3-month escrow + 14-day accelerated cure + 6-month cap (or 30% remaining alternative) by Mon Mar 20. If yes, we'll include the operational SLO table Aditya and Marissa are drafting.

Appreciate the urgency — we'll prioritize getting this to you tomorrow.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
